The old sign_response was ENTIRELY client-authored: every field was a constant, attacker-chosen, or copied verbatim out of the sign_request the server had just returned. Walking the rejection table named by x-rejectionCodes, a synthesised response passed every one and committed, writing a chain entry attesting a human signature by a client-chosen name at a client-chosen time. The tamper defence worked because nothing changed between sign request and commit; the forgery succeeded for exactly the same reason, and a digest comparison cannot tell 'human signed and nothing changed' from 'nobody signed and nothing changed'. The absence of any E_NOT_SIGNED code was direct evidence there was no state machine. FIX: server state open -> answered(signed|declined) -> committed | expired; signed_by from the SESSION COOKIE, at from the SERVER CLOCK; the `signature` object DELETED from commit_request and reduced to `request_id`; request_id added to the snapshot projection (a BREAKING change that must land before the C4 contract freeze, not after). ALSO: S5 ships BOTH hold modes behind one switch from the start — suspend-until-signed, and the two-call {status:'awaiting_signature', ticket} handshake — because V4 decides which is viable and discovering that on Day 4 is a rewrite. V4 HAS DECIDED (MEASURED 2026-08-29, 22.3 s, R-43): the HANDSHAKE is the shipped position and the suspend arm is this node's negative control, expected unrunnable against the built-in browser. The switch still exists — that is why this is a switch position and not a rewrite — but do not build suspend as the default and do not film it. The revoked-tool set is computed from `annotations.readOnlyHint !== true`, never hard-coded: in S2-emp-draft-clean that is SEVEN tools, not five (R-20; `x-freeze.does[0]` in the frozen signature schema still names five and omits submit_expense_report and open_expense_report — that sentence is wrong and this file is the authority). HANDOVER §5: 'the human sign gate is our differentiator' is RETRACTED — webmcpui claims that line publicly. What survives is the mechanism. R-13, AND THIS IS THE HONEST PART OF THIS NODE. A SECOND forgery survives R-1 and is open today. The attacker POSTs /respond itself with the session cookie and the digest the server just issued, then commits; every code named by x-rejectionCodes was walked and none fires, so the commit succeeds. This is inside our own N-04 threat model — curl, session cookie, no browser — and it is scripted as N-16 above. THE ONLY PROVABLE SENTENCE IS: 'a commit cannot be made without a POST from the authenticated session to /api/sign/{id}/respond.' Every stronger headline is DELETED and may not be restored anywhere: not 'a commit cannot be made without a human decision', not 'Layer 0 answers did a human decide', and no `forgeryClosed` flag. WHAT R-1 BOUGHT AND WHAT IT COST: the attacker loses the ability to choose the name and the timestamp, because both now come from the session and the server clock. THE confirm_token IS DEFENCE IN DEPTH, NOT A PROOF: it raises the cost of the attack and it does not establish personhood.
